brief_context: Part of the IEE centre name mentioned in the speech.
brief_extract:
WINTER/SPRING, 1939

STANDARDISATION OF VOLTAGES

"IN electricity supply ... are we content to
potter along towards standardisation of systems
and of voltages little by little and bit by bit at
individual discretion?"
Sir Cyril Hurcomb, K.B.E., C.B., Chairman of the
Electricity Commission, asked this question at the
Annual Dinner of the Mersey and North Wales
Centre of the Institution of Electrical Engineers at
Liverpool on November 21st. The rest of his speech
left very little doubt that to tackle the problem in
this way would indicate a policy both unprogressive
and economically unsound.

location_standardised: Europe
brief_context: Mentioned regarding the development of standard railway gauges.
brief_extract:
Progress and co-ordination inevitably demand
standardisation in certain particulars. The develop-
ment of international travel necessitated a standard
railway gauge in Europe, while the amalgamation of
130 British Railway Companies into four reduced
the variety in railway equipment. "In these things, time runs against us." The
Electricity Commissioners will come to no precipi-
tate conclusion, yet time is literally money.

location_standardised: Finchley, London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Mentioned as an example of a district with different voltage.
brief_extract:
The existing 19 different voltages for use in the
home mean that manufacturers, instead of concen-
trating their attention on perfecting appliances and
lamps of different sizes for one standard voltage,
must produce anything up to 19 times this
number. The lack of uniformity in systems and voltages is
an effective deterrent to many possible electricity
consumers, for they doubt the ease and efficiency
of an electrical service when they find on moving
that "something has to be done" to the iron or the
kettle or any other appliance, because the voltage
in, say, Finchley differs from that in Fulham. Still
more irritating and difficult to understand is why
it should vary in adjacent districts, or even on oppo-
site sides of the road!

THE ELECTRICAL AGE. WINTER/SPRING, 1939
THE CITY OF CARDIFF
By G. H.

location_standardised: United Kingdom
brief_context: Geographic context for the city of Cardiff.
brief_extract:
ALLIN
[Image of City Hall]
THE CITY HALL
UNDERSTAND that the Electrical Association for Women is to hold its Annual Conference in our beautiful city in May next, and I am certain that the members will be very heartily welcomed and that they will thoroughly enjoy their visit. I can quite imagine many of them saying to themselves "but why that dirty, smoky place?" It has to be confessed that amongst people who have never been in our city this impression does exist, and the object of this article is to correct it, because in actual fact Cardiff is one of the cleanest and loveliest cities in the United Kingdom. Although an entirely modern city of 227,000 inhabitants, whose industrial history dates back only about 90 years, Cardiff's actual history can be traced to the Roman occupation, for remains can still be seen of the original Roman Fortress.

location_standardised: Cardiff Castle, Cardiff, Cardiff, Wales, United Kingdom
brief_context: Historical site owned by the Marquis of Bute.
brief_extract: Although an entirely modern city of 227,000 inhabitants, whose industrial history dates back only about 90 years, Cardiff's actual history can be traced to the Roman occupation, for remains can still be seen of the original Roman Fortress. After the Norman Conquest another strong fortress was erected to guard the little town, and, thanks to the Marquis of Bute, the owner of Cardiff Castle, this Norman Keep (as it is styled) has been restored to its original form and can be seen within the Castle grounds. With the discovery of the immensely rich South Wales Coalfield came the birth of Cardiff as we know it to-day.

brief_extract: This first part of the journey often meant half-a-day's strain and struggle for the bullocks and endless patience and cunning from the driver. The river had to be crossed by means of two punts, one in front of the other.

location_standardised: Rome, Provincia di Roma, Lazio, Italy
brief_context: Mention of electricity tariffs for housewives in Rome.
brief_extract:
In those countries where women's sole place is considered to be the home it is consistent that a housewife's whole energies should, as Mr. Parker

put it, "be taken up with sweeping floors with a broom, cooking with a coal or coke fire and cleaning the smuts from her furniture so that she will not have time to be dissatisfied with her lot or question the wisdom of a dictator's decrees."
It is understandable "that the fires, vacuum cleaners, water heaters, refrigerators and other appliances which are common necessities to many Londoners are unattainable luxuries to housewives of similar classes in Berlin, Vienna and Rome."
Advantages are of little use unless followed up, and that is what the E.A.W. as a women's organisation is doing.

location_standardised: Italy
brief_context: Italy surpasses other countries in industrial use of electricity.
brief_extract: We agreed with Mr. Parker "that a fair share of the Roman matron's traditional qualities is required to face the electricity bills!" Italy surpasses any other country in its industrial use of electricity, so that for domestic purposes it is used for very little besides lighting. There is this compensation, however, that extensive railway electrification enables one to complete a long journey more or less as clean as when one stepped into the train.

location_standardised: Vienna, Wien, Austria
brief_context: Mention of electricity service and compatibility in Vienna.
brief_extract: In the matter of service the London housewife scores. Here prompt, efficient attention at the electricity showrooms, hire and hire purchase facilities, and the guarantee of reliable apparatus, are a sine qua non, but in Vienna they are not compatible with middle-class incomes, although in Paris the housewife's needs are met enthusiastically. In contrast to conditions abroad, the comparatively stable incomes and fairly cheap electricity in this country enable manufacturers, without incurring undue risk, to produce apparatus of good design and durability to meet the ever-increasing domestic demand.

There are now about forty factories in production, and tenants have been secured for about as many more. THE PENNY FERRY

It was the presence of the electric power station already established at this spot which played a large part in influencing the Commissioner and his consultants in choosing Treforest as the ideal site.

Ltd., are among the representatives of the world of electricity. POINTER TO PROSPERITY

Already goods of a type never before made in Britain are being exported, and, although such a place as Treforest naturally cannot hope to solve the unemployment problem in the South Wales Special Area, at least it is able to point the way along the high-road to prosperity, and to wield a powerful influence towards a general industrial revival by its example. But now, driving after dark into Kampala, its capital, one is greeted by a blaze of electric street lights and illuminated buildings, which make a rather primitive and insignificant little town look almost like a Riviera resort. Unfortunately, though, that is only an illusion and the introduction of domestic electricity to Uganda has been, and still is, rather uphill work.

brief_context: Mentioned as part of 'London Regional' radio station wavelength analogy.
brief_extract:
THIS may seem a contradictory title, or at the most
another way of saying “turn out the light.” That,
however, is not its meaning; it is concerned with
a process which, shorn of technicalities, holds out
fascinating possibilities for lay folk and is known to the
lighting expert as “fluorescence.”
Sunlight is composed of rays of light in all the colours
of the rainbow, and we are able to recognise these
different colours because each has a different wavelength,
very much in the same way as wireless stations. We
can tune in to the London Regional, for instance, be-
cause it is a different wavelength from the National,
and, similarly, we see yellow as opposed to green for
exactly the same reason. Of all the colours, red has the
longest wavelength, and this is followed by orange,
yellow, green and blue rays, until, finally, we reach the
violet rays which have the shortest wavelength.

brief_extract: Wide possibilities for the use of these lamps exist on the stage, and nearly everybody by now has seen dancers, xylophonists or other performers with part of their costumes treated in this way, appearing brightly lighted against a black background. Anyone who recently saw Henry Cotton, the golfer, at the London Coliseum will remember that the golf balls and clubs he used were fluorescent, while his hands and feet were covered respectively in fluorescent gloves and shoes. The effect of movement and colour on an otherwise darkened stage is very beautiful, but there is no reason at all why fluorescence should not be extended to the auditorium itself, for then the many beautiful decorations which are normally lost during the performance could be softly visible the whole time.

At the Business Session afterwards a discussion on " What is Meant by being Electrically Minded? " resulted in the decision to send the following Resolution to the Appropriate Authority for their action:—
" THAT a National Committee be set up to examine further the question of tariffs for domestic purposes and to make recommendations for their co-ordination."

article_title: Commentary: The Marchioness of Aberdeen and Temair
brief_extract:
SUMMER, 1939
Commentary
The Marchioness of Aberdeen and Temair
WOMEN the world over were saddened to learn of the death on April 18th of the Marchioness of Aberdeen and Temair, G.B.E., LL.D., but their grief was fraught with a joyous remembrance of a life that was rich in blessing to all whom it touched, and none came into contact with her without personal realisation of a wonderful personality and remarkable capabilities dedicated to human welfare and particularly that of women. Lady Aberdeen identified herself with her husband's political sympathies and ideals of public service, and during his Governor-Generalship of Canada and Lord Lieutenancy of Ireland, devoted herself tirelessly to improving social conditions. Long is the list of such services which she initiated.

location_standardised: Derbyshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: A county where experiments with rural electrification were pioneered.
brief_extract: It gives the farmer information as to available supplies and probable costs, and sums up his requirements and represents them to the local Supply Authorities. The Derbyshire Rural Community Council is one of the most go-ahead bodies in this movement, and it was in this county that the experiments with electricity on the farms were pioneered in co-operation with the Derbyshire and Nottinghamshire Electric Power Company. So successful has the venture proved since it was started nine years ago that already over 1,200 farms in the area are now electrified.

location_standardised: Ashford-in-the-Water, Derbyshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: A village where concealed lines were used to preserve beauty.
brief_extract: So successful has the venture proved since it was started nine years ago that already over 1,200 farms in the area are now electrified. The link which originally led to the close liaison with the electricity company in making Derbyshire "electrically minded" was the desire of the Rural Community Council to safeguard the beauties of the countryside from spoliation by the erection of overhead electric lines, with particular reference to the lovely village of Ashford-in-the-Water. As a result of this co-operation it was found that in nearly every case a suitable route could be chosen and the lines erected in concealed positions, so that they would not detract from the charm of the countryside.

brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE. SUMMER, 1939

MEALS
ON
WHEELS
By ALUN JOHN

From the coke stove used in the first dining car in Great Britain in 1879, travelling kitchens have progressed to the electrical efficiency of to-day. "FIRST or second luncheon, please?" Those who have tra- velled any distance on a modern British railway have probably heard this phrase echoing along the corridors of the train, and back again.

location_standardised: King's Cross, London, Greater London, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Origin station for the first dining car in 1879.
brief_extract: Cooking on trains in the early days must have been a ticklish problem. On the first dining car in Great Britain, which ran between King's Cross and Leeds in November, 1879, the cooking was done by means of a coke stove. From that, however, travelling kitchens have gradually progressed to oil, gas and electricity.

brief_extract:
THE ELECTRICAL AGE. AUTUMN, 1939

THE VILLAGE SPEAKS

THE voice of the villages and hamlets of Britain has been heard by most of us this summer, speaking with a different inflexion, from the soothing slurred speech of the West Country, the soft tones of Sussex and the Downs, the invig- orating burr of the North, the slow rounded drawl of East Anglia, the precise lilt of Wales, and the forceful rhythm of Scotland. They have told the same lovely tale for centuries and they will go on telling it, but from thatched Cotswold cottage to slate-grey Cornish farmstead, there is an element still required to make the charm of their song com- plete.

fairyland.
